dave_customer: Hey @alice_support — we just got a customer escalation (ticket #INC-12345). They report p99 for streaming endpoints jumped from ~1.2s to ~6s last night. TTFB looks fine but the total time is spiky. Repro steps below, attaching a minimal curl test that reproduces in our staging region.

alice_support: thanks @dave_customer. can you paste the curl + headers you used and any request IDs from the response? also which client (SSE / websocket / h2) did they use?

incidents-bot: Alert: streaming-response-p99 spike detected for tenant tenant-42 in us-west-2 (alertid: a-9c8f).

 dave_customer: they use SSE via our public API. sample curl I used:

```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" "https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/stream?model=rw-13b" 
```

Behavior: first chunk arrives ~150ms, then a 4–6s gap, then chunks resume. Repeats unpredictably. request_id in response header: r-202603170901-abc123 (one example).

alice_support: good, that's enough to start. tagging @ben_eng and @carol_sre to help investigate edge/proxy behavior. can someone grep proxy logs for r-202603170901-abc123 and paste the edge -> backend timing?

ben_eng: grabbed the trace. edge->ingress accepted request at 23:14:11.100, backend accepted at 23:14:11.130, first chunk from backend at 23:14:11.250 (KV cache hit), then no further chunks until 23:14:15.400. backend did stream more data at 11:14:15.380 but edge didn't forward until 11:14:15.400 — tiny, but consistent with coalescing/flush window. stack: envoy h2 multiplexer + custom coalesce window at edge VCL.

carol_sre: we rolled a policy change to increase coalesce window last week to reduce small-chunk overhead (saw token cost savings). looks like tenant-42's workload has bursty mid-stream output causing p99 regressions for long-tailed clients.

ben_eng: yep — reproduced locally by toggling coalesce window. reproducer: run with coalesce_ms=200 -> see 4s mid-stream gap for certain sequence of chunk sizes. with coalesce_ms=0 the gaps vanish.

```
# quick repro snippet
./stress-client --model rw-13b --prompt-file small-bursty.txt --coalesce-ms 200
# observe: first event, long silence, then remainder
```

carol_sre: mitigation options: 1) tenant override to set coalesce_ms=0 for tenant-42, 2) add short-term SDK fallback: use non-streaming endpoint for requests with <X tokens, 3) temporary canary to reduce coalesce globally (not ideal).

alice_support: customer prefers streaming, they just want stable p99. would tenant override be safe for rollback?

ben_eng: yes — tenant-level overrides are supported. we can flip a flag in edge-config to disable coalescing for tenant-42, rollback in 5m if problems. will affect cost for that tenant slightly.

eva_devex: also worth adding a quick note in the JS SDK about forcing SSE -> non-streaming fallback when experiencing mid-chunk stalls; but that's a medium-term change.

carol_sre: deploy plan: 1) stage toggle for tenant-42 in staging; 2) apply to prod at 23:50 with monitoring; 3) keep for 24h and gather p95/p99 metrics; 4) follow up with a postmortem decision on permanent rule. I can run the rollout and rollback.

alice_support: sounds good. @dave_customer can you message the customer to confirm we will try the tenant override and ask if they can accept a short maintenance window?

dave_customer: pinged them, they said yes, please proceed.

ben_eng: applying override now (edge-api call):

```
POST /edge-config/overrides
{
  "tenant": "tenant-42",
  "overrides": {"coalesce_ms": 0}
}
```

...done. propagation to edge nodes started.

incidents-bot: Change deployed: edge override for tenant-42 (coalesce_ms=0). rollout status: 12/12 nodes updated.

ben_eng: initial telemetry: p99 for tenant-42 stream endpoints dropped from ~5.8s -> ~1.3s within 2 minutes. p95 stable.

alice_support: excellent. logging this as mitigation in the ticket, will keep monitoring. assign follow-up to @ben_eng + @carol_sre for postmortem and cost analysis.

carol_sre: action items: 1) quantify cost delta for tenant-42 with coalesce disabled, 2) determine whether we can make heuristic: disable coalesce for bursty prompts automatically, 3) add dashboard for coalesce window regressions.

ben_eng: also adding unit test for streaming flush behavior to catch regressions in coalescing change.

alice_support: customer confirmed improvement. closing escalation; we'll keep ticket open pending postmortem in 72h. :thumbsup:

ben_eng: short term note for engs: if you need to reproduce locally, use stress-client above or run curl with `--no-buffer` on clients and set coalesce_ms on edge to see the window.

dave_customer: thanks everyone. will update customer and copy postmortem when ready.
